components.name: Solid Content Card
components.description: A solid light card that floats over the scroll gradient so text stays legible over any part of it.

Content overload

components.name: Contents Rail Dot
components.description: Signature in-page navigation — fixed vertical dot rail in teal; active dot grows and its label fades in.

components.name: Research Section Band
components.description: A full-width flat coloured band, one per part of a study; text sits directly on the colour, no box. Bands cycle dark → neutral → tint, using a per-study trio.

narrative.overview: The whole system reads as clean, breathable air that a warm haze gradually creeps across — you only notice it when it thickens. The neutral clear-air ground is the default; amber is the heat that builds (urgency that accumulates rather than shouts); teal is the quiet recurring accent that carries the beneficial side of the story; dust is the softer warm haze that ties the pages together. This serves the argument: secondhand AI is two-sided, its effects are invisible and hard to spot, and it carries an urgency felt more than announced. The signature moment is the overview's scroll gradient: the background hazes clear-air → amber as the reader descends. Elsewhere the same logic is flat coloured section bands (research) or a single quiet ground with colour carried in the type (index, examples). It rejects the SaaS landing page, the paper-as-webpage look, and AI-panic clickbait.
keyCharacteristics: Clear-air neutral is the default ground; colour is used sparingly and deliberately
Amber = heat/urgency, dust = softer warm haze, plus teal as the single recurring accent on every page
The overview's live scroll gradient hazes clear-air → amber as you descend
Research pages are flat coloured section bands built from exactly three colours
Wave-shaped dividers stitch the coloured bands; surfaces are kept clean of decorative line art

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent on every page; it carries links, navigation, and the beneficial side of the two-sided story.

rules.name: The Amber-Is-Heat Rule
rules.body: Amber means urgency, heat, or the harm side — never decoration. Keep it rare so it still reads as heat.

rules.name: The Quiet-Ground Rule
rules.body: Clear air is the default. Colour is added deliberately, never wall-to-wall.

rules.name: The Flat-Band Rule
rules.body: Section backgrounds are flat and never carry a shadow; anything lifted is a solid light card on top.

rules.name: The Legible-Card Rule
rules.body: Any content card over the amber-transitioning gradient must be a solid light surface with dark text, never a translucent tint.

rules.name: The Title-Owns-the-Fold Rule
rules.body: Abril Fatface is the wordmark alone; Archivo carries all headings; Public Sans carries everything else. The title commands attention only because the display face stays rare and the supporting fonts stay quiet.

dos: Do keep clear air as the default ground and add colour deliberately.
Do keep teal as the one accent on every page, carrying links, nav, and the beneficial side.
Do use amber only for heat, urgency, or the harm side — and keep it rare.
Do build research pages as flat coloured bands from exactly three colours in the fixed order.
Do run the overview background as a clear-air → amber scroll gradient with content on solid light cards.
Do give every non-index page a "← Back to index" link and a prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
donts: Don't introduce a generic SaaS landing-page look — no hero-metric tiles, gradient text, per-section eyebrows, or identical card grids.
Don't let the site read like an academic PDF — stage research as coloured bands and designed scenes.
Don't tip into AI-panic clickbait — there is no red alarm; amber is warmth that rises, not danger.
Don't put dark text on amber sections or light-grey text on light grounds.
Don't use more than three band colours on a single research page.

Don't use Abril Fatface for anything but the wordmark, add a fourth family, or use numbered markers as decoration. The system is Abril Fatface (wordmark) + Archivo (headings) + Public Sans (everything else).
